add.title: Rwanda's transgender community face violent detentions for being trans (VICE World News)
add.summary: VICE World News (20 Nov 2020): although being transgender is not criminalised in Rwanda, police routinely arrest trans women on pretext charges — 'homelessness', drug sales, theft — and detain them at Kigali's Gikondo Transit Center, a facility for people exhibiting 'deviant acts or behaviors'. Bella was held there after police falsely claimed she was homeless and sold drugs; as punishment she was confined in a tiny dark cell known as 'the cat box' and raped by fellow detainees at least three times. Gabi was detained at Gikondo for six months in 2018; Nunu was detained there three times between 2018 and 2019. Detainees are supposed to be charged within 72 hours or transferred to a police station, court, rehabilitation facility, or jail, but trans detainees are held for indeterminate periods in facilities lacking transparency. Documents placement practice: trans prisoners are held under a 'deviance rehabilitation' framework in transit centres (with segregated/confining cells used as punishment), not in facilities matching their gender identity.

add.title: Outright International: Rwanda country page
add.summary: Thin-to-useful: Outright's Rwanda page (updated March 2026, based on a July 2025 Human Rights First Rwanda Association submission to the UN Human Rights Committee) reports transgender individuals face heightened risks of harassment at identity checks and arbitrary arrests on grounds such as 'vagrancy' or 'public order' offenses, and that LGBTIQ people flee arbitrary arrests, detention and ill-treatment. It corroborates the detention pattern for trans people but gives no prison-placement (men's vs women's facility) detail.
